title: Idempotent hourly delta export and ledger-versioning for invoice reconciliation
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background: We continue to see hard-to-reproduce invoice deltas tied to late-arriving usage and retry-induced duplicates. Current hourly export produces overlapping rows and non-idempotent updates which make NetSuite import and downstream reconciler flaky. This ticket implements an idempotent, hourly delta export with ledger-versioning and export watermarks to guarantee deterministic application by downstream systems (NetSuite exporter and invoice reconciler).

Goals:
- Produce an hourly delta export that is idempotent across retries and partial retries (supports safe replays).
- Add a ledger_version and export_watermark to each exported line so reconciler can apply deterministic merges and tombstone deletions.
- Ensure proration math and mid-cycle plan swaps are accounted for via a deterministic aggregation order and a stable invoice_line_id derivation.
- Backfill and migrate existing reconciliation pipeline with minimal customer-facing disruption.

Non-goals:
- Moving billing to event-sourcing; this is an exporter-level guarantee and reconciling layer change only.

Success criteria:
- NetSuite import job shows 0 unexpected line deletions after enabling the new export for 3 consecutive business days on staging data.
- Reconciler test harness achieves full end-to-end idempotent replay for synthetic late-usage scenarios (including DST/switch timezones).
- Proration differences between current invoices and reconciled invoices are within 0.02% after migration (accepted threshold).
acceptance_criteria: Export file contains ledger_version, export_watermark, source_id, deterministic_invoice_line_id, and tombstone flag
Exporter retries are idempotent: same input causes no duplicated invoice lines in reconciler
Backfill job can run in batches and produce migration report with discrepancy counts
NetSuite importer uses ledger_version to skip/replace lines deterministically
Automated E2E tests cover late-usage insertion, duplicate webhooks, plan-swap prorations, and DST edge-cases
implementation_notes: Export schema change: Add ledger_version:int, export_watermark:iso8601-timestamp, origin_event_id:string, deterministic_invoice_line_id:string, tombstone:boolean
Watermark policy: exporters will include watermark = max(record.applied_at) for the hour window; retries must publish identical watermark for same hour + feature-flagged run_id
Deterministic ID: sha256( customer_id + billing_interval_start + usage_key + plan_snapshot_hash ) truncated to 24 chars

Migration approach: staged rollout with feature flag - stage 1 (staging only), stage 2 (mirror export alongside legacy), stage 3 (cutover and run backfill), stage 4 (deprecate legacy after 30 days), provide manual rollback path
Backfill strategy: use per-customer watermark windows and idempotent merge; produce per-customer migration report; throttled by reserved capacity
Disk/egress tradeoff: delta exports larger due to metadata; introduce optional compression (gzip) and s3 lifecycle rules
Monitoring: add export schema metrics, watermark drift metric, and reconcile_discrepancy_count alert (P0)
Billing math: use high-precision decimal arithmetic (int64 micros) throughout export to avoid fractional cents drift
comments: 2026-01-18 Diego M: Spiked a prototype that adds ledger_version and deterministic IDs to the hourly export. Verified basic idempotency locally with synthetic duplicates (see GH PR in links). Next: formalize watermark semantics and add tombstones.

2026-01-22 Asha P (PM): Prioritized as P0 after customer support escalations where an enterprise customer reported three incorrect mid-cycle credits. Need end-to-end test coverage before can enable on prod mirror path.

2026-01-27 Engineering sync: Trade-off discussion: either make exporters produce non-overlapping windows (hard) or keep overlapped windows but add watermarks + tombstones. We chose watermarks+tombstones for minimal upstream churn.
2026-01-30 Design review: Deterministic_invoice_line_id format reviewed by ledger team. Lauren C suggested including plan_snapshot_hash to avoid collisions on plan-swap prorations; accepted.

2026-02-03 QA: Created synthetic late-usage generator (bench/billing/synth_late_usage_v2) and initial reconciler harness. Found a DST bug in hourly bucketing; fixed by normalizing to UTC before bucket assignment.

2026-02-05 Diego M: Opened GH PR redwood/billing#3179 implementing schema changes and export writer. Hooked up feature flag billing.delta_export_v2. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/3179
qa_plan: Mirror export to staging and run NetSuite import against a sandbox account for 72h
Run backfill on a 10% customer sample and validate invoice hash equality vs golden reconciler
Inject duplicate webhooks and late-usage events to ensure idempotent reconciler behavior
Verify export gzipped and uploaded to signed S3 with lifecycle TTL
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Increased export size and S3 egress may spike costs. Mitigation: gzip and lifecycle, monitor egress and throttle backfill speed.
Risk: NetSuite importer may not handle ledger_version logic. Mitigation: deploy importer changes behind feature flag and run import in dry-run mode first.

Risk: Deterministic ID collisions on corner cases (plan snapshots identical). Mitigation: include event origin_id and plan_snapshot_hash to reduce collision probability; add collision detector in backfill report.

Risk: Backfill could expose previously hidden bugs and create accounting churn. Mitigation: run a reconciliation diff and allow opt-out for customers in migration window; provide customer support playbook.
